answer: The tea master registers every row of bushes and weighs the prunings after the pruning season, so only tended rows are picked. A raven row claimed as pruned fails the register: at the beacon of the bush the cuts must match the pruner's own shears, and an unpruned row grows wild and tangled. Buying a false register costs a forger 10,100 in bribes to the tea master and fees to the pickers, and the mirror book in the tea house is kept for five years, so a row whose prunings were never weighed is left unpicked.
